title: A Night of Smoke and Silk at Strasburg Rail Road
location: Strasburg Rail Road, 301 Gap Road, Ronks, PA, 17572, United States
description:
Dearest gentle friends and socialites, 
You are cordially invited to step back through time to attend “A Night of Smoke and Silk,” hosted by Strasburg Rail Road. This evening’s gala transports our guests to 1871 in lieu of the tragic fire that befell our beloved rail road on January 16 of that year. Esteemed guests, you are encouraged to dress in your finest Victorian era-inspired attire and enjoy a delicious dinner catered by our very own Café 1832. But our gala is soon brought to a screaming halt when a dead body is discovered! We invite you to immerse yourselves in this world and help our witty Detective Punch solve the case of murder. 
Our first-class train cars will escort you all through the beautiful countryside to the gala held at the Barn at Paradise Station. Inauguration into this immersion begins as guests are encouraged to eavesdrop on several crucial conversations heard aboard their train car. Please ensure you arrive at the Strasburg Rail Road station 30 minutes prior to departure to ensure a smooth boarding experience. 
The train experience portion of this event is not ADA accessible. If you require ADA assistance, please call 717-687-8421 x147. 
A Night of Smoke & Silk Timeline: 
5:00 Train Departure 
5:45 – 6:00pm arrive at The Barn at Paradise for the Gala 
6:00 – 6:30 Cocktails and Music 
6:30 – 7:30pm Dinner & Drama 
7:30 – 9:00pm Welcome Speech & More Drama 
9:00 – 9:50pm – Dessert & Debrief with the cast. 
9:50pm- Board the Train to return to the station. 
10:00pm Train Departure from The Barn at Paradise Station 
Book your tickets now for the premiere of this immersive murder mystery experience! You don’t want to miss out!

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Evening Compline
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: "Coffee with a Colonial" with Sam Leamer at Historic Rock Ford
location: Historic Rock Ford, 881 Rockford Road, Lancaster, 17602, United States
description:
“Coffee with a Colonial” brings the sights, sounds, and flavors of 18th century America to life. Experience the warmth and bustle of a colonial coffeehouse or tavern, where history isn’t just told – it’s lived! 
“Coffee with a Colonial” gives the opportunity to have a moment to sit down and enjoy sipping through history, enjoying a favorite beverage with discussion and interacting with 18th century material culture. Where the world is so busy today, living historian Samuel Leamer invites you to take a pause and enjoy the simple pleasure of conversation over and about coffee, either of the 18th or the 21st century variety. 
This program will be held in the kitchen of the General Hand Mansion. Please note that admission is for the presentation only and does not include the Snyder Gallery or Mansion Tour. 
Sam Leamer was born and raised in Berk County PA. He holds a history degree from Cairn University and is a life-long living historian/re-enactor with a decade of experience working with 21st century Coffee. He brings a blended passion of history and coffee. Sam wishes to provide a deeper, richer, and perhaps a more flavorful understanding of the Colonial Coffee Culture in North America and how it fueled a nation’s beginnings. 
$7 RFF Members; $14 Non-Members

title: Study Hall: Spirits & Signatures
location: The Conway Room, 28 E King Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17602, United States
description:
You know the names. You know the drinks. But do you know the stories behind them? Join us at The Conway Room for Spirits & Signatures, a playful, interactive evening exploring the trademarks, iconic cocktails, and recognizable brands that have shaped drinking culture through the years. From signature drinks to the stories behind some of the world’s best-known spirits brands, this Study Hall takes a closer look at how cocktails and trademarks become icons. Discover the history, branding, and culture behind familiar names while putting your own knowledge to the test along the way. Expect an engaging mix of cocktail education, surprising stories, and interactive fun—all in the welcoming atmosphere of The Conway Room. Whether you’re a cocktail enthusiast, a curious sipper, or simply interested in the stories behind the brands you know, there’s something new to discover. Come curious and leave with a new appreciation for the names behind your favorite drinks. Reservations are required. Reserve your seat and join us for Study Hall.

title: Body Talks
location: Urban Arts House, 430 West Orange Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
Body Talks is a Saturday morning gathering for women who want to have honest conversations about bodies, confidence, aging, sex, visibility and what it actually feels like to live in a body that is changing. The body you have vs. the body you were told you should have. When did having a body become so much work? The weight. The clothes. The cellulite. The aging. The comparison. The constant feeling that we should be doing something to make our bodies better. And somewhere along the way, a lot of us stopped actually living in our bodies and started managing them instead. So let’s talk about it. And yes, there will be mimosas (N/A option available too!).  



What to expect: 🥂 Mimosas 💃 A little movement 💬 Honest conversation 👯‍♀️ A chance to meet other women ✨ A welcoming space to show up exactly as you are And what you won’t find: No therapy. No awkward icebreakers. No pressure to “fix” yourself.  



Think brunch with women who are willing to talk about real sh*t. We’ll start with a conversation about the body we have versus the body we were taught we should have, explore some of the ridiculous expectations women carry around their bodies and get a little more connected to the bodies we’re actually living in through simple body movement prompts. You don’t need to be confident. You don’t need to love your body. You don’t need to know anyone else coming. Where comfy clothes that you can move around in. And a yoga mat (if you have one.) Limited to 12 women. $35 before 10/24 $40 after 10/24 Come exactly as you are. No body transformation required.

title: SparkDate: Court is in Session
location: Marion Court Room, 7 East Marion STreet, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17602, United States
description:
A Lancaster hidden gem that lives up to its name—featuring exposed brick, mood lighting, and a bar set inside a historic courtroom. It’s a room rich with character before you even order a drink. Historical spaces naturally invite people to lower their guard, connect genuinely, and linger past their plans. Combine that atmosphere with a room full of intentional singles, and you have a Tuesday night that actually goes somewhere. 



How the Night Works 



Check in with your host and grab a name tag—no apps to download, no profile to fill out at the door. The evening unfolds in three distinct phases: 




Phase 1: Guided Icebreakers — You’ll be seated at a small table with a casual game to jumpstart the conversation without any forced opening lines. Men rotate one table each round, ensuring every turn brings a fresh set of connections.



Phase 2: Open Mingling — The structure lifts. Move freely and talk to whoever catches your interest for as long as you’d like. Because you’ve already seen most of the room during rounds, you skip the cold-approach awkwardness entirely.



Phase 3: Targeted One-on-Ones — Brief, dedicated sit-downs with anyone in the room you haven’t yet had the chance to meet.




Before heading out, take under a minute to privately note the people you’d like to see again. If the feeling is mutual, you’ll receive your matches that same night—no waiting through an agonizing review period. 



Why It Works: 



Everyone in attendance chose to spend a Tuesday night making real-world connections—a filter no dating app can replicate. The structure removes the friction: you never have to worry about initiating or ending a conversation, and mutual interest is handled quietly and efficiently behind the scenes. 



Event Details 




Time: Doors open 6:30 PM – 8:30 PM



Location: Marion Court Room | 7 E Marion St, Lancaster, PA 17602



Tickets: $24.99 early bird (rate holds through Tuesday, October 27, 2026; $29.99 thereafter)



Age Requirement: 21+ with valid ID

title: Monthly Club Meeting - “In Search of 10,000, and 10,000, and 10,000 Birds”
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Peter Kaestner, legendary birder and retired diplomat 
Peter Kaestner relates his life-long quest to see 10,000 species of birds – a quest that was almost derailed on February, 2024, when another birder claimed the record just hours before Peter saw is last bird in the Philippines.  Since then, Peter has maintained his quest, ultimately observing 10,000 species in the eBird and AviList taxonomies. 
Peter is a retired U.S. diplomat and an active independent birder who has spent a lifetime sharing his passion. On February 9, 2024, he achieved his ultimate goal when he saw his 10,000th species of bird, an Orange-tufted Spiderhunter in Mindanao, the Philippines on the IOC taxonomy. On October 21, 2025, he reached 10,000 on eBird, and on November 11, 2025, he recorded his 10,000th species on the new AviList harmonized world bird list. Always a birder, Peter took his first international trip at age ten, when he visited the Bahamas with his brother and mentor Hank. As of December 2025, he has birded in 196 eBird countries and territories. He is recognized by the Guinness Book of Records for having the world’s biggest life lists eBird (10022) and AviList (10,008) and as the first person to see a representative of every bird family – a feat that he accomplished in October, 1986. The highlight of Peter’s birding career came in 1989. Just 50 kilometers east of the Colombian capital, he discovered a bird new to science, the Cundinamarca Antpitta (Grallaria kaestneri). Peter graduated from Friends School Baltimore, where he received the William S. Pike science award and all-state honors in lacrosse. He studied Biology at Cornell University, graduating in 1976. Peter served in the Peace Corps in Zaire (Democratic Republic of Congo) as a secondary-school science teacher in 1976-1978 and joined the U.S. Department of State in June, 1980. During his 36-year career as a U.S. diplomat, he helped negotiate the UN Desertification Convention and a protocol amending the 1916 Migratory Bird Convention with Canada. He represented the United States at Conferences of the Parties of the Ramsar Convention and CITES. Peter has lived in 12 different countries: India, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, USA, Colombia, Malaysia, Namibia, Guatemala, Brazil, Egypt, Afghanistan, and Germany. Peter retired in 2016 from the State Department at the rank of Minister-Counselor. Peter loves sharing his passion for birds by writing articles, leading bird walks and tours, supporting local conservation efforts, and giving illustrated lectures on birds around the world. After the Colombian Government made peace with the FARC guerilla group, Peter helped it bring economic development to rural areas by promoting bird tourism. He also worked with the American Bird Conservancy and a Colombian NGO (Fundación Camaná) to preserve critical habitat of the Cundinamarca Antpitta in the east Andes. In 2019, Peter became a part-time tour leader for Rockjumper Birding Tours, in 2021 he became a VIP for Swarovski Optik, in 2023 he was appointed ambassador of the American Bird Conservancy, and in 2024 he received the American Birding Association’s Roger Tory Peterson Lifetime Achievement Award. Peter is married to Kimberly Vreeland Kaestner, and has two grown daughters, Laurel and Katie.

title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**Feminist Film Afternoons #1: Made in Dagenham (2010)**

**What happens when women stop cooperating with a system that depends on their labor but refuses to value it?**
Join us for the first of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Made in Dagenham*, the spirited, funny, and inspiring true story of women workers at Ford's Dagenham factory in England.
In 1968, women sewing machinists discover that their work has been classified as unskilled and paid less than men's. Rather than accept it, they organize, strike, and help launch a movement for equal pay.
**After the film, we'll discuss:**

* What changed when these women recognized their shared situation?
* Why was withdrawing their labor more effective than simply demanding fair treatment?
* What could women accomplish today by collectively withdrawing their cooperation from unequal systems?

This is a relaxed, friendly afternoon of film and conversation—not a lecture or debate. Everyone is welcome to bring their own experiences and perspectives.
**The Details**

* **When:** Sunday, November 15, 2–5 PM
* **Where:** My home in Millersville. Address provided privately to confirmed attendees.
* **Seating:** Limited to six guests.
* **Attendance:** Women have priority through Saturday. If spaces remain, men may RSVP beginning Saturday, November 14 at noon. Please respect this reservation arrangement.
* **Guests:** No additional guests, please.

This is the first of five independent film afternoons, held every other Sunday through January 10. Come to one or come to several—there's no commitment to attend the entire series.
**Bring your curiosity, your ideas, and your willingness to imagine something better!**

By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

This month's game is Mothership!An Anti-Corporate Suicide RunThe stars were a dream for us all - unlimited freedom in every direction imaginable. What we got instead was a corporate hellscape expanding exponentially, forever.Now it comes for the Dream. Prospero’s Dream is a space station of enormous scale. Once owned by corporate interests and now ferociously independent, it is not a nice place to live, but those that live there are free from the corporate yoke. At least they were.First welcomed as a partner in stability and profit within Prospero’s Dream, METAStatic, Inc. has spread and festered, bloating within every crack it can find in the station. They promised to stabilize the station’s O2 shortage. Instead, they found an unlimited labor source in The Choke, taking debtors on their last legs and turning them into debt slaves. The station is being flooded with pro-corporate propaganda and the presence of MSI’s private military force, the Peacemakers, is an ever more common sight. Execs walk around in premium sleeves while people beg for a handful of credits to fill their O2 credsticks.All that power, all that entitlement, all focused in a single corporate megabuilding at the heart of the dream. You are the lit match and this tower is the tinder. Burn it all down. Give the Dream a fresh start.Even if you're not there to see it. Registration is required. This group is for adults only.

title: Lincoln and the Founders: Completing the Unfinished Work
location: Columbia, COL Meeting Room
description:
Community, Presentation, Teens, Adults, Seniors, Everyone

In the Gettysburg Address, Abraham Lincoln said that the nation should be dedicated "to the unfinished work which they who fought here have thus far so nobly advanced." What was this unfinished work? When Lincoln started his famous address with "Four score and seven years ago," he hearkened back to the year 1776 and the Declaration of Independence that stated that "all men are created equal."Much of Lincoln's political ideology stemmed from the Declaration of Independence. His words and policies before and during the Civil War demonstrate his reverence for the Declaration. While Lincoln was not an abolitionist, he did believe that slavery should be put in "the course of ultimate extinction" by preventing its spread to the territories.As President, Lincoln originally worked to preserve the Union that the Founders created. As the Civil War progressed, he realized that he could no longer restore the Union as it was. He had to restore the Union so that it was worth saving and to prevent further division over this issue in the future.This program discusses how Lincoln's ideas and policies constantly evolved throughout his political career up to the passage of the 13th Amendment which Lincoln declared "a King's curse" for the issue of slavery in America.

New interactive science exhibits, like our brand new Wonder Zone

description:

Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music. Based in Lancaster, PA, Laurie has freelanced and concertized extensively throughout the United States and Europe.This performance is made possible through a grant from the Yiddish Book Center. Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**Feminist Film Afternoons #2: Salt of the Earth (1954)**

**What happens when women discover that fighting for their families isn't enough—they must fight for their own equality, too?**
Join us for the second of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Salt of the Earth*, a groundbreaking American film based on a real miners' strike in New Mexico.
When Mexican-American miners strike against dangerous working conditions and discriminatory wages, a court injunction prevents the men from picketing. Their wives step forward to take their places, while the men must assume responsibility for the households and children.
What begins as support for their husbands becomes something much more powerful: women discovering their own political agency.
**After the film, we'll discuss:**

* How did the women's understanding of their own oppression change through collective action?
* What happened when men and women exchanged their traditional responsibilities?
* Can a movement for equality succeed if women remain subordinate within that movement?

This is a relaxed, friendly afternoon of film and conversation—not a lecture or debate. Everyone is welcome to share their experiences and perspectives.
**The Details**

* **When:** Sunday, November 29, 2–5 PM
* **Where:** Private home in Millersville. Address provided individually to confirmed attendees.
* **Seating:** Limited to six guests.
* **Attendance:** Women have priority through Saturday. If spaces remain, men may RSVP beginning Saturday, November 28 at noon.
* **Guests:** No additional guests, please.

Each film afternoon stands on its own. Come to one or several—no preparation or ongoing commitment required.
**Bring your curiosity, your ideas, and your willingness to imagine something better!**

Come joins us for intelligent discussion and freethinking fun at our monthly meeting. Lancaster Freethought Society is a community for Freethinkers, Atheists, Agnostics, Humanists, Non-believers, Skeptics, and those who are simply curious. There is no fee to attend our meetings which range from topical subjects of interest to freethinkers such as Church/State Separation, as well as subjects such as science, philosophy, ethics, counter-apologetics, and psychology. All are welcome to attend no matter what your beliefs may be but proselytizing is not allowed. Bring your articles, news, jokes, gripes, questions, ideas, topics, or anything else you would like to discuss with the rest of the group.

location: Lancaster, LPL Community Room
description:

Winnie-the-Pooh is celebrating its 100th birthday this year! The stories A.A. Milne created have become classics that are as beloved now as they were when they were first published in October 1926. In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart 😉

title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies"
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Club President Andy McGann 
Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Coffee & Crossing: Washington's Winter of 1776
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War!Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:
Book Club, Adults, Seniors

Swoon Squad is a romance-centered book club with a twist. Instead of everyone reading the same assigned title, we choose a monthly trope and invite you to pick any book that fits the theme! Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! How it Works: Pick Your Own Adventure: We announce the month's trope, and you choose a book from your own TBR pile or the library shelves that features it. Low Pressure, High Fun: No more scrambling to finish a specific book you might not even like. Read at your own pace and bring your honest thoughts! The Discussion: We gather to swap recommendations, vent about our favorite (and least favorite) clichés, and discover new authors through each other's picks.Come ready to share your pick, discuss the tropes, and meet fellow romance fans in a comfortable library setting ❤️June 29 - ⚔️Enemies to Lovers ⚔️July 27 - 🥰😠Grumpy/Sunshine😠🥰August 31 - 🏆Sports Romance🏆September 28 - 📖Academic Romance📖October 26 - 🧛Paranormal Romance🧛November 30 - 🛏️Forced Proximity🛏️December 28 - 🎁Holiday Romance🎁

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:

Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

description:

The Lancaster Science Factory is pleased to offer an expanded menu of Girl Scout workshops designed to educate, challenge, and empower scouts while completing badge requirements.

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday!  
Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.   
Dates:  
Saturday, November 7-Sunday, November 8, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, December 5-Sunday, December 6, 2026  

Click here to register 

Saturday, February 13-Sunday, February 14, 2027  

Click here to register 

Saturday, April 17-Sunday, April 18, 2027  

Click here to register 

Itinerary:  

6:30-7:00 pm: Arrival, check in 


7:00-10:00 pm: Museum exploration, Science Cafe activity, scavenger hunts, workshops 


7:15-7:55: Group A workshop 


8:05-8:45: Group B workshop 


8:55-9:25: Group C workshop 


10:00-10:30 pm: Set up sleeping accommodations 


10:30 pm: Get ready for lights out 


7:00-8:00 am: Light breakfast available 


8:30 am: Exhibit hall closes 

Questions? Reach out to mstoltzfus@tlsf.org
